settings.headline:
Code review,
without the backlog.
settings.copy: LintLine drops an AI reviewer into your pipeline that reads every diff for security holes, logic errors, and style drift — in seconds, not days. Your humans review the interesting stuff.

settings.title: Everything a senior reviewer
settings.intro: LintLine combines static analysis with a reasoning model that understands intent, so it flags real problems instead of style nitpicks.

features.title: Security scanning
features.text: OWASP-aware checks for injection, auth bypasses, secrets in code, and dependency vulnerabilities — surfaced inline on the diff.

features.title: Logic & edge-case review
features.text: The model traces control flow to find off-by-one errors, null dereferences, and race conditions that linters miss entirely.

features.title: Style & consistency
features.text: Enforces your team's conventions across every file, so reviewers stop arguing about formatting and start about architecture.

features.title: Inline suggestions
features.text: Every finding comes with a concrete, merge-ready suggestion and a one-line explanation of why it matters.

features.title: Auto-approve safe changes
features.text: Trivial refactors and docs get approved automatically, routing only meaningful changes to a human.

features.title: Team coverage reports
features.text: See review velocity, recurring issue patterns, and where senior time is actually going — weekly, on your dashboard.

settings.title: From push to reviewed

steps.title: Connect your repo
steps.text: Install the LintLine GitHub/GitLab app and pick the repositories you want reviewed. No changes to your CI required.

steps.title: We read the diff
steps.text: On every pull request, LintLine fetches the changed files and runs its security + reasoning review against your ruleset.

steps.title: Comments appear inline
steps.text: Findings post directly on the diff with severity, a suggested fix, and a plain-English explanation.

steps.title: Safe changes auto-approve
steps.text: Trivial work merges itself. Anything meaningful waits for your team's human review, already triaged.

steps.title: Your team learns faster
steps.text: Repeated patterns surface in the insights dashboard, so the whole team stops making the same mistakes.

settings.note: LintLine never stores your code. It analyzes in-memory and keeps only the findings and statistics.

settings.title: Your reviewers should be doing
settings.image_caption: Review findings surfaced inline, triaged by severity

paragraphs.text: Most review time is spent on things a machine should catch: formatting, missing null checks, a secret that slipped into a config file. Every minute on that is a minute not spent on design and architecture.
LintLine absorbs the mechanical 70% so your senior engineers review only what actually needs their judgment. The result is faster merges, fewer escapes, and a review process people stop dreading.

settings.quote: The best reviewer is the one who only shows up for the hard parts.

settings.title: Simple plans

settings.title: Questions, answered
settings.intro: The honest answers to what teams ask before adopting LintLine.

items.question: Does LintLine replace human code review?
items.answer: No. It absorbs the mechanical 70% — security, style, obvious logic errors — so your humans spend their time on architecture and design. Your senior reviewers are the gate on anything that matters.

items.question: Is our code stored or used to train models?
items.answer: No. LintLine analyzes each diff in-memory and retains only findings and statistics. We never train on your proprietary code and never store source.

items.question: Which git hosts do you support?
items.answer: GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket — both cloud and self-hosted. Enterprise can run LintLine fully inside their own VPC.

items.question: How is this different from a linter?
items.answer: A linter checks rules. LintLine reasons about intent — it traces control flow to catch logic errors and security issues that no rule list covers. It's a reviewer, not a formatter.
